overall_reason: The skeleton is the familiar SaaS order (logo strip, feature bento, integrations hub, case-study stats, testimonial wall, CTA), but almost every section carries a product-specific demonstration in Cal's own typeface and neutral palette: UI chips set inside the h1, a working booking widget on a desktop mock, a real email-thread problem, attributed named customers; the generic parts are a few headings and the testimonial wall.

findings.evidence: T-STOCK-ORDER counts 8 stock sections in stock order: hero with product mock -> logo strip ('The fastest-growing companies use Cal.com for scheduling') -> 3-step problem/solution tabs -> feature bento ('One calendar for every way people meet.') -> integrations hub -> case-study stat pills -> testimonial wall -> CTA/footer. Each section is executed with specific product content, which is why the read stays 'made' with medium confidence.
findings.before: Default SaaS sequence, 1844 words over ~13 screens
findings.after: Cut the sections that restate others (the testimonial wall repeats the case studies; the integrations hub repeats the feature bento) so the page ends after the proof
findings.why: Specific content on a default sequence still reads partly as template; the length dilutes the strong first three screens.

findings.evidence: Failed T-FRESH-READER on heads: "All your key tools in sync with your meetings.", "Scheduling for absolutely everyone.", "See why our users love Cal.com. Read the impact we've had from those who matter most: our customers." These fit Calendly or SavvyCal unchanged (T-RIVAL-NAME).
findings.after: Lead with a quoted fact from a named customer, e.g. the Navi line about health information, as the heading
findings.why: Heads that any rival could run are the generic layer on an otherwise specific page.

findings.evidence: Masonry of 15+ testimonial cards with avatar circles; several quotes are pure superlative ('Thrilled with this scheduling app—it's a game-changer... seamless scheduling and top-notch customer service', 'One of the best tools for scheduling'); sources are named handles on X, Trustpilot and Product Hunt (real attribution, so not invented).
findings.before: Wall of generic praise cards behind 'Show more'
findings.after: Keep 3 quotes that state a specific outcome or switch ('made the move... couldn't find how to edit events in the calendly dashboard'); link each to its source post
findings.why: A testimonial wall is a look-family tell; the specific, sourced quotes carry it, the superlatives dilute it.

findings.where: case-study stat pills and problem section, tiles 02 and 08
findings.evidence: 'Deel spends 35% less time scheduling... and gets back more than 6,000 hours a week'; pills 'From $500M to $1.5B+ ARR', 'From 12s to <2s page loads', '50% more demo efficiency'. Each links to a case study ('Read the story'), but the ARR figure is the customer's growth, not Cal's effect.
findings.before: "From $500M to $1.5B+ ARR" as a Cal.com result
findings.after: State what Cal changed for that customer [DATA NEEDED: the scheduling metric from the Deel case study]
findings.why: Borrowed customer growth figures read as an outcome claim; keep the stat that is causally Cal's.

strengths: The h1 'Where [photo] people [Intro call 30m ✓ Booked] find [NYC clock] the time to meet' sets live product chips inside the headline: a device no default produces; keep it.
The problem section shows an actual email thread ('Re: Re: Intro call? Thursday at 10 then?') next to 'Four people, three time zones, eleven emails and still no slot.': picturable and falsifiable.
Product demo is the real booking page (Rick Astley 'Get Rickrolled' event, Europe/London, 12h/24h) inside a Windows desktop mock: playful and only-Cal.
Brand typeface (Cal Sans) and restrained neutral palette are consistent and owned.
not_investigated: Several images render as broken or beige placeholders (avatars, Salesforce and Google Meet icons, case-study video area, events demo): capture blocked scripts and two fonts (manifest network), so these are not judged as design.
Animated hero chips and tab auto-advance seen as stills only.
